feature_results.rationale: GitHub documents repository-configured JSON hooks that execute user-supplied shell commands at session, prompt, pre-tool, post-tool, and agent-stop events. The preToolUse hook can approve or deny any tool execution, meeting the action-influence criterion rather than merely sending passive notifications.

evidence.excerpt: Hooks are a way of executing custom shell commands at strategic points in an agent's workflow, such as when an agent session starts or ends, when you enter a prompt, or when a tool is called.
**preToolUse**: Executed before the agent uses any tool (such as `bash`, `edit`, `view`). This is the most powerful hook as it can **approve or deny tool executions**.

constraints.description: The cited mechanism is documented for Copilot cloud agent on GitHub and Copilot CLI in the terminal; this evidence does not establish identical support in every IDE.
Repository hooks are defined in .github/hooks/*.json. Hooks execute synchronously and block agent execution; the default command timeout is 30 seconds.

queries: GET https://docs.github.com/en/copilot (known source; followed its About hooks navigation)

feature_results.rationale: Copilot cloud agent has a configurable outbound firewall with organization and repository allowlists for domains and URLs. Owners can enforce organization rules, control repository customization, and enable or disable the firewall. This is a network-specific execution control, not merely process isolation.

evidence.excerpt: By default, Copilot's access to the internet is limited by a firewall.

Items added to the organization custom allowlist apply to all repositories in the organization. These items cannot be deleted at the repository level. Organization-level and repository-level rules are combined.

constraints.description: The documented cloud-agent firewall operates only inside the GitHub Actions appliance, not processes outside it; this evidence does not establish equivalent controls for local IDE or CLI agents.
Applies to processes started via the agent's Bash tool, not directly to MCP server processes or configured setup steps. GitHub warns sophisticated attacks may bypass it.
Cloud agent is documented as available for all paid Copilot plans; enterprise and organization access policies can restrict its use.

feature_results.rationale: VS Code documents a checkpoint restore that reverts affected workspace files and conversation history across subsequent requests in one operation, rather than requiring per-file or per-hunk undo. CLI also offers prompt-level conversation-and-files rewind across later turns. This is session-wide rollback of tracked agent work, not reversal of external side effects or an unrestricted machine snapshot. An inconsistent warning in the CLI concept page does not establish broader restoration coverage; the operational how-to and VS Code checkpoint documentation substantiate the narrower supported scope.

evidence.excerpt: VS Code removes subsequent requests from the conversation history and restores the workspace files to their state at the checkpoint.

Choosing a rewind point opens an action menu where you can select **Conversation only** or **Conversation + files**. The latter is unavailable for a rewind point when neither that turn nor any later turn changed any files that can be restored.

constraints.description: Verified mechanisms are VS Code Restore Checkpoint and local interactive Copilot CLI /undo or /rewind; CLI rewind is unavailable for remote-backed or busy sessions.
VS Code checkpoints restore affected workspace files and chat history, not completed commands, network requests, deployments, or external-service changes; checkpoints are temporary.
CLI file restoration requires file tracking, skips later user-modified files and files over 10 MB, and cannot restore a turn with more than 500 changed files.

feature_results.rationale: Administrators can monitor policy and access changes using audit logs, and cloud-agent session logs and audit events are available to administrators. Copilot usage metrics additionally expose enterprise, organization, repository, and user-level API reports and exports. These are organizational controls rather than personal history; documentation establishes Business as well as Enterprise governance, not an Enterprise-only logging restriction.

evidence.excerpt: Session logs and audit log events are available to administrators.
Use your audit log to monitor changes to policy settings or organization enablement.
The Copilot usage metrics APIs, which provide detailed, exportable data at the enterprise, organization, repository, and user levels.

constraints.description: Organizational governance applies to Copilot Business and Enterprise license holders. Personal plans do not supply organization administration.
Usage metrics exclude Copilot Chat on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile. Rich IDE metrics require enabled end-user telemetry; agent-app breakdowns appear in APIs and exports, not dashboards.

Metrics documentation lists minimum IDE and Copilot Chat extension versions, including VS Code 1.107.1 with extension 0.35.3, Visual Studio 17.14.13 with 18.0.471.29466, and JetBrains 2024.2.6 with 1.5.52-241.
Report data can take two full UTC days after a day closes. Visibility follows enterprise/organization roles, including the custom View organization Copilot metrics permission.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot has a dedicated review product that analyzes pull requests and suggests fixes, not merely an ad hoc chat request. Automatic PR reviews can be configured by users, repository owners, or organization owners. The PR-hosting workflow meets the full criterion.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot reviews your pull requests, identifies issues, and suggests fixes you can apply in a couple of clicks.
In repositories where automatic code review is enabled, Copilot automatically reviews all pull requests.

constraints.description: Personal automatic reviews are documented for Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise licenses. Free does not include code review. Business/Enterprise organizations can separately enable paid reviews for members without a license.
Review is supported on GitHub.com, GitHub CLI, GitHub Mobile, VS Code, Visual Studio, Xcode, and JetBrains IDEs. Personal automatic reviews are unavailable for managed user accounts.
Core code review is generally available; Azure DevOps support and passing suggested fixes to the cloud agent are public preview.
The review product uses a tuned mix of models; user model switching is not supported.
Agentic full-project context gathering uses GitHub Actions runners. If its workflows fail or runners are unavailable, the review falls back to a more limited review.
Organization policy must enable code review for organization-provided access on GitHub.com and Mobile. Re-review on new pushes requires configuration or a manual request.

feature_results.rationale: An official worked example uses a single project-level natural-language refactoring prompt to centralize logging, create a logging aspect, update main.py, and remove duplicated logging from multiple service classes. The documented result preserves the logging operations while restructuring their implementation. This is AI-driven multi-location restructuring, not merely a symbol rename or an IDE-native command; correctness of any particular generated refactor still needs testing.

evidence.excerpt: @workspace Refactor this project by using AOP to avoid logging that has cross-cutting concerns
Copilot then tells you to remove the logging code from all of the service classes, and gives you the code for the revised files.
In the refactored version of the project, the same logging operations are performed, but the logging code is centralized in a single file.

constraints.description: The worked example uses VS Code or Visual Studio with @workspace; the page specifies @project instead for JetBrains.
The documented responses are non-deterministic examples, not a guarantee of behavior-preserving output for every project.

queries: site:docs.github.com/en/copilot refactor code extract function restructure multiple files GitHub Copilot tutorial

feature_results.rationale: Official IDE guidance explicitly documents /tests generating tests for an active file or selected code, with optional framework and edge-case instructions. It also documents test-first generation for code that has not yet been written. This is a named test-generation capability rather than incidental general code generation.

evidence.excerpt: Use the `/tests` slash command to ask Copilot to write tests for the active file or selected code.
The `/tests` slash command writes tests for existing code. If you prefer to write tests before writing code (test driven development), omit the `/tests` command.

constraints.description: The fetched examples document /tests for VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, and Eclipse; this evidence does not establish the same command in every Copilot surface.
Copilot Chat access is required. An organization can disable Chat for its members.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI autopilot carries out successive task steps without waiting for further user instructions. IDE agent mode independently selects files, edits them, executes commands and iterates; cloud agent plans and implements delegated tasks. This is general multi-step execution, not a fixed predefined workflow.

evidence.excerpt: Autopilot mode allows Copilot CLI to work through a task without waiting for your input after each step. Once you give the initial instruction, Copilot CLI works through each step autonomously until it determines the task is complete.
In agent mode, Copilot takes a high-level task, decides which files to change, makes the edits, and runs commands as needed, iterating until the task is done.

constraints.description: CLI autopilot pauses after five automatic continuation messages by default; the limit is configurable. Actions requiring permissions cannot proceed unless permissions are granted; manual approval mode automatically denies those tool requests during autopilot.
IDE agent mode is documented for VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Xcode and Eclipse; commands require approval by default unless editor or administrator settings permit automatic execution.
Agent availability and usage allowance depend on plan and organization policies; all plans include CLI and app, with limited agents on Copilot Free.

feature_results.rationale: Cloud agent researches, plans and implements delegated changes in the background while the user continues working. It requests review when coding work finishes. This satisfies asynchronous task execution independently of narrow background test or terminal-command support.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot cloud agent can research a repository, plan changes, and implement them in the background.
When Copilot finishes a coding task and requests your review, check the pull request thoroughly before merging.

constraints.description: The verified asynchronous mechanism is Copilot cloud agent on GitHub-hosted repositories; repository owners and administrators may disable it.
Each cloud agent session has an unextendable maximum execution time of 59 minutes; a run operates in one repository on one branch and can open one pull request.
Human review and merge remain required; GitHub Actions workflows on agent pull requests require approval by default.

feature_results.rationale: Repository semantic indexing is explicitly used to answer natural-language codebase questions with relevant code references. Cloud agent also automatically retrieves code by meaning rather than exact grep matches. This establishes repository-wide semantic retrieval, not merely substring search or active-file context.

evidence.excerpt: When you start a conversation with Copilot Chat that has a repository context, the repository is automatically indexed to improve context-enriched answers to your questions about the code's structure and logic in GitHub and Visual Studio Code.
Copilot cloud agent uses semantic code search to find relevant code based on meaning, rather than relying solely on exact text matches with tools like `grep`.

constraints.description: The repository index is documented for Copilot Chat in GitHub and VS Code, and for Copilot cloud agent. Availability in other IDEs should not be inferred from these statements.
Semantic indexing of non-GitHub workspace repositories is supported in VS Code on GitHub.com, not GHE.com or GitHub Enterprise Server, and uploads workspace data to GitHub.
Non-GitHub semantic indexing is disabled by default; Business/Enterprise administrators must explicitly enable its policy. Chat context is filtered by applicable content exclusions.

feature_results.rationale: Users can author Markdown/YAML custom agent profiles with independent prompts and tool allowlists, optionally including MCP server configuration. The documented CLI /agent creation flow explicitly permits restricting tools, and custom profiles can be instantiated as subagents with separate context windows.

evidence.excerpt: You define custom agents using Markdown files called agent profiles. These files specify prompts, tools, and MCP servers.
By default, custom agents have access to all tools. If you restrict an agent's access, a `tools` specification is added to the agent file.
One of the benefits of using custom agents you have defined yourself—or the built-in agents—is that the main Copilot agent can run them as subagents with a separate context window.

constraints.description: The verified creation and delegation mechanism is Copilot CLI. Custom-agent support and maturity vary across IDEs in the known feature matrix.
CLI-created project profiles live in .github/agents/ and user profiles in ~/.copilot/agents/. The creation guide instructs users to restart the CLI to load a new profile.
When run as subagents, custom agents do not follow repository custom instructions by default; include-custom-instructions: true opts them in.

feature_results.rationale: Official documentation provides native non-MCP registration surfaces: the Copilot SDK defines callable tools with argument schemas and handlers and passes them through session tools configuration. Copilot CLI extensions can also register tools into an existing interactive session through joinSession. This satisfies the documented API/config criterion; the CLI extension surface is explicitly experimental, not undocumented.

evidence.excerpt: Let's give Copilot the ability to call your code by defining a custom tool.

The single call to `joinSession` is what turns a plain Node.js file into a Copilot CLI extension. It connects the running process to your session and registers everything the extension adds to the CLI—in this case, a single tool.
**`handler`**—an async function that runs when Copilot calls the tool. Whatever string it returns becomes the tool's result, which the model reads.

constraints.description: Verified surfaces are SDK-powered applications and Copilot CLI interactive-session extensions, not an assertion of a universal tool-registration interface across Copilot IDEs.
CLI extensions are experimental and require --experimental or /experimental on.
CLI extension entry modules must be JavaScript run by Node.js; TypeScript and other languages are not currently supported for that extension entry surface.
SDK custom tools require the Copilot SDK and an installed/authenticated CLI; the Node.js, Python, and .NET SDKs provide the CLI automatically.
A registered extension tool is available for model selection but cannot mandate that the agent call it.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency exposes the Restrict Copilot to data residency compliant models policy. Enabling it keeps inference processing, code, prompts, responses, and related logs/telemetry within the designated US or EU geography. This is an actionable regional restriction for processing as well as storage, not just a default location. The generic DPA's international-transfer permission does not override this more specific product control.

evidence.excerpt: Your code, prompts, and Copilot responses never leave your region during inference processing.
To enable this policy, use the **Restrict Copilot to data residency compliant models** policy in the "Features" section of your enterprise's Copilot policies.

constraints.description: Requires an enterprise using GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. The policy is disabled by default; enforced requests consume 10% more AI credits.
Supported designated regions are the United States and European Union.
Only region-certified, region-available models are surfaced; models hosted outside the designated region cannot be accessed. Regional model lists differ and can lag new global releases.

Business/Enterprise data is contractually protected from training without customer authorization, and that personal toggle is not displayed for these plans. This establishes the actionable training opt-out branch of the feature; it does not imply universal zero retention of prompts, responses, session logs, or telemetry.

Select the "Allow GitHub to use my data for AI model training" dropdown menu and click **Disabled**.
GitHub will not use Inputs or Outputs to train generative AI models, unless you have given us documented instructions to do so.

feature_results.rationale: Cloud agent has documented built-in dependency validation against the GitHub Advisory Database, with analysis and actions visible in its session log and identified issues fed back into remediation. This meets the database-backed integration criterion. The confirmed scope is newly introduced dependencies and malware/High/Critical findings, not an assertion that every existing dependency or vulnerability severity is scanned continuously.

evidence.excerpt: Newly introduced dependencies are checked against the **GitHub Advisory Database** for malware advisories, and for any CVSS-rated High or Critical vulnerabilities.
Details about the analysis performed and the actions taken by Copilot cloud agent can be reviewed in the session log.
It attempts to resolve issues identified prior to completing the pull request.

constraints.description: The built-in scanning evidence applies to Copilot cloud agent, not every Chat, CLI, or editor completion workflow.
Documented scanning is limited to newly introduced dependencies, malware advisories, and CVSS-rated High/Critical vulnerabilities. Ecosystem coverage is not enumerated on this page.
Cloud agent security validation does not require an additional Secret Protection, Code Security, or Advanced Security license.
Validation tools are enabled by default but repository administrators can disable them.

feature_results.rationale: VS Code documents an opt-in edit approval workflow that displays a diff and asks for approval or rejection before an edit is applied. This meets the strict pre-write requirement when the relevant paths require approval. Separate Local-harness review supports individual inline edits, rather than only whole files. However ordinary pending Keep/Undo edits are already saved, and Agent Host applies edits directly, so those default post-write workflows alone do not qualify. The status is scoped to the configurable pre-apply approval workflow, not all Copilot surfaces.

evidence.excerpt: To prevent inadvertent edits to files such as workspace configuration or environment settings, VS Code can show a diff and ask you to approve or reject the edit before it is applied.
Use the chat.tools.edits.autoApprove setting to configure which files require approval. The setting uses glob patterns to match file paths in your workspace.
Hover over an inline change to accept or reject that specific change without affecting other edits in the file.
Pending means that you can keep or undo the saved edit. It doesn't mean that the edit is waiting to be written to disk.

constraints.description: Pre-apply diff approval is documented in Microsoft's first-party VS Code documentation. Do not generalize it to other IDEs, CLI sessions, or cloud-agent changes.

Configure chat.tools.edits.autoApprove glob rules to require approval for relevant files. Pre-apply approval is distinct from post-save Keep/Undo and does not establish coverage of writes through terminal commands, scripts, or external tools.
Per-edit Keep/Undo is documented for Local extension-host sessions. Agent Host has no equivalent pending per-edit review state; its edits are applied and saved directly.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI documents actually performing commits and reverts, not merely suggesting commands. The GitHub surface also handles branch creation, commit messages, and pushes.

evidence.excerpt: Use Copilot to help you perform Git operations.
Commit the changes to this repo
When implementing changes, Copilot handles branch creation, commit messages, and pushing changes.

constraints.description: CLI commands that modify or execute files normally request tool permission; explicit approval options can scope which Git operations are allowed.

feature_results.rationale: Official documentation provides non-interactive prompts, permissions, prevention of clarification prompts, JSONL output, and CI examples. Fully documented exit-code semantics are available specifically for the direct dynamic-workflow CLI mode: success 0, incomplete/error 1, missing workflow or invalid arguments 2, interruption 130. This establishes a qualifying unattended structured-output mode without extrapolating those exit codes to ordinary -p sessions.

evidence.excerpt: This allows you to use Copilot programmatically in scripts, CI/CD pipelines, and automation workflows.
With `json`, the CLI emits JSONL (one JSON object per line), which is convenient for parsing the agent's output in scripts.
The command does not display permission approval prompts.
The workflow was not found, or its arguments could not be read, parsed as JSON, or validated against the workflow's accepted inputs.
**Use `--no-ask-user`** to prevent the agent from attempting to ask clarifying questions.

Authentication and necessary tool permissions must be configured before execution. The documented 0/1/2/130 exit-code table applies to workflow run; ordinary prompt-session exit codes were not established by these pages.
An unsuccessful workflow can leave an old result file intact; check the exit code before consuming it. Errors before startup or interruptions may omit a final JSON record.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot automatically generates grayed inline suggestions as the developer types, including complete function bodies, without a chat prompt. Current IDE documentation describes partial-line, whole-line, and larger-block suggestions. The feature matrix lists completion support in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode, and NeoVim. Numerous languages are supported rather than a documented narrow language subset.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot will automatically suggest an entire function body in grayed text. The exact suggestion may vary.
Suggestions can complete part of a line, an entire line, or a larger block of code.
GitHub Copilot provides suggestions for numerous languages and a wide variety of frameworks, but works especially well for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, Go, C# and C++.
| Code completion |✓ |✓ |✓ |✓ |✓ |✓ |

constraints.description: Copilot Free limits inline completions to 2,000 per month.
Completion support is listed for VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode, and NeoVim; this is editor integration, not a chat-only or terminal feature.
The matrix describes latest IDE/extension versions and recommends latest stable versions; it is not an assurance for every historical version.

feature_results.rationale: Original Copilot documentation verifies an Allow/Block public-code matching setting and withholding matches or near matches. Current March 2026 organizational AI terms extend defense of third-party claims to outputs only when the customer's main agreement already provides that defense; they do not constitute an unconditional indemnity for every plan.
